strings.d1.s0.name: Acropolis of Athens
strings.d1.s0.tips: The Parthenon: book an online timed ticket for the 08:00 opening (30 EUR, or 36 EUR for the 7-site combined ticket). In summer it may close between 12:00 and 17:00 because of the heat.
strings.d1.s1.name: Acropolis Museum
strings.d1.s1.tips: A museum with glass floors, the Parthenon frieze and a cafe with views of the Acropolis.
strings.d1.s2.name: Plaka
strings.d1.s2.tips: Neoclassical streets at the foot of the Acropolis, plus the white Cycladic-style houses of Anafiotika.
strings.d1.s3.name: Kostas Souvlaki Syntagma
strings.d1.s3.tips: One type of souvlaki only since 1950; on Agia Irini square, closes at 14:00.
strings.d1.s4.name: Anafiotika
strings.d1.s4.tips: An island village tucked against the Acropolis rock: narrow stairways and cats.
strings.d1.b0.name: O Thanasis Monastiraki
strings.d1.b0.tips: A kebab and pitta classic on Monastiraki Square.
strings.d1.b1.name: Areopagus Hill
strings.d1.b1.tips: A rocky hill beside the Acropolis; free views and a good sunset spot.
strings.d2.s0.name: Ancient Agora of Athens
strings.d2.s0.tips: Enter with the combined ticket. The Temple of Hephaestus is the best-preserved Greek temple, and the Stoa museum is also worth a look.
strings.d2.s1.name: Monastiraki Flea Market
strings.d2.s1.tips: The antiques market sets up on Sundays; on other days the shops are open. Avissinias Square.
strings.d2.s2.name: Roman Agora & Tower of the Winds
strings.d2.s2.tips: Combined ticket; an octagonal water-clock tower.
strings.d2.s3.name: Varvakios Central Market
strings.d2.s3.tips: The central meat and fish market; the tavernas inside serve patsas (tripe soup) and grills.
strings.d2.s4.name: Psyrri
strings.d2.s4.tips: A graffiti-covered district: cafes and Little Kook by day, taverns in the evening.
strings.d2.b0.name: Diporto Varvakios
strings.d2.b0.tips: A basement taverna with no menu; chickpeas and fish, cash only.
strings.d2.b1.name: Kerameikos
strings.d2.b1.tips: An ancient cemetery; the combined ticket is valid, and it is quieter than the Roman Agora.
strings.d3.s0.name: Mount Lycabettus
strings.d3.s0.tips: Take the funicular or climb for 20 minutes. It is the highest point in Athens, with views of the Acropolis and the sea.
strings.d3.s1.name: Kolonaki
strings.d3.s1.tips: A chic neighbourhood; try the cafes on Skoufa street.
strings.d3.s2.name: Benaki Museum
strings.d3.s2.tips: A mansion of Greek history and crafts, with a terrace cafe.
strings.d3.s3.name: National Archaeological Museum
strings.d3.s3.tips: The Mycenaean gold mask and the Antikythera mechanism; air-conditioned for the midday heat.
strings.d3.s4.name: Exarcheia
strings.d3.s4.tips: An anarchist and student district with record shops and rebetiko bars.
strings.d3.b0.name: Philos Athens Kolonaki
strings.d3.b0.tips: Brunch in Kolonaki: lunch instead of a museum.
strings.d3.b1.name: Museum of Cycladic Art
strings.d3.b1.tips: Cycladic idols; an alternative to the Benaki.
strings.d4.s0.name: Lake Vouliagmeni
strings.d4.s0.tips: One hour by tram and bus; a thermal lake with fish pedicures, 22°C even in winter.
strings.d4.s1.name: Astir Beach Vouliagmeni
strings.d4.s1.tips: A stylish Riviera beach; sunbeds included, clear water.
strings.d4.s2.name: Ithaki Restaurant Vouliagmeni
strings.d4.s2.tips: Seafront fish restaurant; a Riviera classic.
strings.d4.s3.name: Glyfada Centre
strings.d4.s3.tips: The Riviera's shopping district; return by tram.
strings.d4.s4.name: Flisvos Marina
strings.d4.s4.tips: A waterfront walk and sunset at the marina, plus the Averof battleship.
strings.d4.b0.name: Akrogiali Vouliagmeni
strings.d4.b1.name: Stavros Niarchos Foundation Park
strings.d4.b1.tips: A Renzo Piano park and opera house; an alternative to Flisvos.
strings.d5.s0.name: Lavrio Archaeological Museum
strings.d5.s0.tips: A town of ancient silver mines, on the way; 1.5 hours from Athens by KTEL bus.
strings.d5.s1.name: Akrogiali Sounion Taverna
strings.d5.s1.tips: A fish taverna on the bay, with views of the temple.
strings.d5.s2.name: Sounion Beach
strings.d5.s2.tips: A cove below the temple; swimming in summer.
strings.d5.s3.name: Temple of Poseidon Sounion
strings.d5.s3.tips: A temple on the cape. Arrive at 17:30 for sunset (16:30 in winter), and look for Byron's signature on a column.
strings.d5.b0.name: Cape Sounion Sunset Cafe
strings.d5.b0.tips: A cafe next to the temple.
strings.d5.b1.name: Lavrio Harbour
strings.d5.b1.tips: A fishing harbour; an alternative to the museum.
strings.d6.s0.name: Hydra Port
strings.d6.s0.tips: 1.5 hours by fast ferry from Piraeus (about 30 EUR); a car-free island of donkeys and stone mansions.
strings.d6.s1.name: Hydra Kamini Walk
strings.d6.s1.tips: Walk the coastal path to the village of Kamini; there are rocky swimming platforms.
strings.d6.s2.name: Hydra Spilia Beach
strings.d6.s2.tips: Jump from the rocks into the sea; in summer.
strings.d6.s3.name: Kodylenia's Taverna Hydra
strings.d6.s3.tips: A taverna with sea views in Kamini.
strings.d6.s4.name: Hydra Town Streets
strings.d6.s4.tips: A town laid out like an amphitheatre; the ferry leaves at 17:00.
strings.d6.b0.name: Hydra Sunset Restaurant
strings.d6.b1.name: Hydra Monastery Climb
strings.d7.theme: Panathenaic Stadium, National Garden and a gentle farewell
strings.d7.s0.name: Panathenaic Stadium
strings.d7.s0.tips: A marble Olympic stadium; you can run on the track.
strings.d7.s1.name: National Garden Athens
strings.d7.s1.tips: The former royal garden, with palms and turtles, next to the Zappeion.
strings.d7.s2.name: Syntagma Changing of the Guard
strings.d7.s2.tips: The Evzones change on the hour; a full ceremony takes place on Sundays at 11:00.
strings.d7.s3.name: Ta Karamanlidika tou Fani
strings.d7.s3.tips: A deli and meze tavern; pastirma (cured beef) and a cheese platter make a fitting farewell meal.
strings.d7.s4.name: Syntagma Metro Airport
strings.d7.s4.tips: The airport metro takes 40 minutes; farewell.
strings.d7.b0.name: Feyrouz Athens
strings.d7.b0.tips: Lahmacun (thin Turkish flatbread) and cheese pides; a quick farewell meal.
strings.d7.b1.name: Temple of Olympian Zeus
strings.d7.b1.tips: Combined ticket; giant columns, an alternative to the stadium.
strings.note0: The metro has 3 lines; the airport metro takes 40 minutes and costs 10 EUR. Take the tram to the Riviera, the KTEL bus to Sounion (Pedion Areos) and ferries from Piraeus to the islands.
strings.note1: The Acropolis costs 30 EUR, with online timed entry; the 7-site combined ticket costs 36 EUR and is valid for 5 days. Entry is free on the first Sunday (November to March).
strings.note2: Summer reaches 35-40°C: visit the Acropolis at 08:00, a museum at midday and a Riviera beach in the afternoon. In August the locals are away on the islands.
strings.note3: Souvlaki costs 4-5 EUR and a taverna meal 15-25 EUR; the coffee to order is freddo espresso. Tip by rounding up; there is no coperto (cover charge).
strings.note4: Pickpockets are common on the metro and in Monastiraki; Omonia is deserted at night.
strings.note5: On Sundays there is the Monastiraki flea market and the Syntagma ceremony; museums may be closed on Tuesdays.
